title: Action, Intent, Proposal, Command and Operation
results: Action is not raw transition or causation; it is an attribution over selected behavior/intervention relative to an actor/controller model.
Control Action, Intentional Action and Operational Action/Operation must not be collapsed.
Selection can be policy-based, automated or stochastic without reflective deliberation.
Goal and Intent are distinct; intention has a planning/commitment role beyond target representation.
Intentional commitment and Runtime operational commitment are different semantic kinds.
Proposal is a communicated candidate specification and may be rejected before a committed Operation exists.
Command is an encoded directive/request, not an Action, committed Operation or Effect.
Planning operators/plans and monitored physical execution/outcomes remain distinct.
Operation should be decomposed into type/contract, request/proposal instance and committed operation instance when identity matters.
Operation is distinct from Transition, Effect and Attempt.
Operation identity is richer than command text and context-free parameters.
Delegated action requires explicit separation of planning, proposal, principal, admission, execution, effect-owner and observation roles.
Admission validates/commits an operational contract rather than psychological intent or semantic success.
Current Ordivon ExecutionProposal -> RuntimeExecutionPlan -> Job/operationDigest structure receives foundation-level support.

nextRound.title: Execution, Realization, Effect and Consequence
nextRound.entryQuestion: What does it mean for an identity-bound committed Operation to become concrete behavior, and how are execution lineage, target effect and wider consequence separated?

notes: RF2 explains current proposal/admission/operation semantics but does not authorize API/object renames or Runtime Core changes.
